entities.name: expression or template body used for automatic typing

requirements.subject: ent:automatic-type
requirements.canonical: The automatic type MAY be used only in a variable declaration, a template variable declaration, a constant declaration or a module parameter declaration.
requirements.original: Automatic types are used in variable, constant and module parameter declarations.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence is descriptive; it is unclear whether the list is exhaustive (other declarations, e.g. formal parameters or templates, are excluded) and whether template variable declarations count as variable declarations (the examples use `var template`). Chose the exhaustive reading including template variables.
readings: The automatic type MAY be used only in variable (including template variable), constant and module parameter declarations.
The automatic type MAY be used at least in variable, constant and module parameter declarations; other uses are not addressed.

requirements.subject: ent:declaration
requirements.condition: the declaration uses the automatic type
requirements.canonical: A variable, constant or module parameter declaration that uses the automatic type IS written without the type part.
requirements.original: When used, the type part of these declarations is skipped and the type is provided implicitly.

requirements.subject: ent:automatic-type
requirements.canonical: The type of a declaration that uses the automatic type IS provided implicitly.
requirements.original: When used, the type part of these declarations is skipped and the type is provided implicitly.

requirements.subject: ent:automatic-type
requirements.canonical: The automatic type IS equal to the type of the expression or template body on the right-hand side of the assignment of the declaration.
requirements.original: The automatic type is equal to the type of an expression or template body on the right-hand side of an assignment of the declaration.

requirements.subject: ent:automatic-type-initializer
requirements.canonical: The type of the expression or template body used for automatic typing SHALL be unambiguously determinable from the expression or template body itself.
requirements.original: The type of the expression or template body used for automatic typing shall be implicitly unambiguous.

ambiguity.issue: "implicitly unambiguous" is not defined; it can mean determinable without any type context, or determinable according to the list a) to q). Chose the first reading, which the list then makes concrete.
readings: The type of the expression or template body SHALL be determinable without any external type context.
The type of the expression or template body SHALL be determinable by applying the rules of items a) to q) of clause 6.5.

requirements.subject: ent:automatic-type-initializer
requirements.canonical: The expression or template body used for automatic typing SHALL be one of the forms listed in items a) to q) of clause 6.5.
requirements.original: The expression or template body shall be one of the following:

requirements.subject: ent:automatic-type-initializer
requirements.canonical: The expression or template body used for automatic typing MAY be a reference to an existing variable, formal parameter, constant or template, or to a field or element inside of it.
requirements.original: a) Reference to an existing variable, parameter, constant, template or a field or element inside of it.

ambiguity.issue: "parameter" is used where formal parameter (or module parameter) is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:automatic-type-initializer
requirements.canonical: The expression or template body used for automatic typing MAY be a call of a function returning a value, including a predefined function.
requirements.original: b) Function call returning a value, including predefined functions.

requirements.subject: ent:automatic-type-initializer
requirements.canonical: The expression or template body used for automatic typing MAY be a TTCN-3 operation returning a value, such as `match`, `valueof` or `ispresent`.
requirements.original: c) TTCN-3 operation returning a value such as match, valueof, present, etc.

ambiguity.issue: "present" is not a TTCN-3 operation; the `ispresent` operation is meant. The list is open ("etc.").

requirements.subject: ent:automatic-type-initializer
requirements.condition: the result type can be unambiguously resolved
requirements.canonical: The expression or template body used for automatic typing MAY be an expression composed of several operands whose result type can be unambiguously resolved using the rules for expressions or automatic types.
requirements.original: d) Expression composed of several operands where the type of the result can be unambiguously resolved using the rules for expressions (clause 7) or automatic types.

requirements.subject: ent:automatic-type-initializer
requirements.canonical: The expression or template body used for automatic typing MAY be a literal of the `integer`, `float`, `boolean`, `bitstring`, `hexstring`, `octetstring` or `verdicttype` type.
requirements.original: e) Literal of the integer, float, boolean, bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, verditctype type.

requirements.subject: ent:automatic-type-initializer
requirements.canonical: The expression or template body used for automatic typing MAY be a character string literal.
requirements.original: f) Character string literal.

requirements.subject: ent:character-string-literal
requirements.condition: the literal contains only characters of the charstring type
requirements.canonical: If a character string literal used for automatic typing contains only characters of the `charstring` type, the automatic type IS `charstring`.
requirements.original: If the literal contains only characters of the charstring type, the automatic type is charstring, otherwise it is universal charstring.

requirements.subject: ent:character-string-literal
requirements.condition: the literal contains a character outside the charstring character set
requirements.canonical: If a character string literal used for automatic typing contains a character that is not of the `charstring` type, the automatic type IS `universal charstring`.
requirements.original: If the literal contains only characters of the charstring type, the automatic type is charstring, otherwise it is universal charstring.

requirements.subject: ent:automatic-type-initializer
requirements.canonical: The template body used for automatic typing MAY be an inline template.
requirements.original: g) Inline template.

requirements.subject: ent:automatic-type-initializer
requirements.canonical: The expression used for automatic typing MAY be a qualified enumerated value.
requirements.original: h) Qualified enumerated value.

requirements.subject: ent:value-list-notation
requirements.condition: all values of the value list have a common type
requirements.canonical: A value list notation in which all values have a common type SHALL provide the automatic type `record of` the common type.
requirements.original: i) Value list where all values have a common type shall provide an automatic type record of _{common type}._ The common type shall fulfil requirements for automatic typing.

requirements.subject: ent:common-type
requirements.canonical: The common type of the values of a value list notation used for automatic typing SHALL fulfil the requirements for automatic typing.
requirements.original: i) Value list where all values have a common type shall provide an automatic type record of _{common type}._ The common type shall fulfil requirements for automatic typing.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-notation
requirements.condition: all values in the assignment notation fulfil the requirements for automatic typing
requirements.canonical: An assignment notation used for automatic typing SHALL provide an automatic record type with the same number and order of fields as in the assignment notation.
requirements.original: j) Field assignment notation where all values fulfil requirements for automatic typing shall provide an automatic record type with the same number and order of fields as in the field assignment notation.

ambiguity.issue: "field assignment notation" is used for the glossary term "assignment notation".

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-notation
requirements.canonical: Each value in an assignment notation used for automatic typing SHALL fulfil the requirements for automatic typing.
requirements.original: j) Field assignment notation where all values fulfil requirements for automatic typing shall provide an automatic record type with the same number and order of fields as in the field assignment notation.

ambiguity.issue: "field assignment notation" is used for the glossary term "assignment notation".

requirements.subject: ent:record-field
requirements.canonical: The name of each field of the automatic record type IS equal to the corresponding field name in the assignment notation.
requirements.original: The names of record fields are equal to the field names from the notation and record field types are automatic types of the field values in the notation.

requirements.subject: ent:record-field
requirements.canonical: The type of each field of the automatic record type IS the automatic type of the corresponding field value in the assignment notation.
requirements.original: The names of record fields are equal to the field names from the notation and record field types are automatic types of the field values in the notation.

requirements.subject: ent:record-field
requirements.condition: the field value does not fulfil the present template restriction
requirements.canonical: A field of the automatic record type IS optional if the corresponding value in the assignment notation does not fulfil the requirements of the `present` template restriction.
requirements.original: A record field is created as optional if the value in the notation doesn't fulfil requirements of the present template restriction (see clause 15.8 for more details), otherwise it is created without the optional property.

requirements.subject: ent:record-field
requirements.condition: the field value fulfils the present template restriction
requirements.canonical: A field of the automatic record type IS NOT optional if the corresponding value in the assignment notation fulfils the requirements of the `present` template restriction.
requirements.original: A record field is created as optional if the value in the notation doesn't fulfil requirements of the present template restriction (see clause 15.8 for more details), otherwise it is created without the optional property.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.condition: all indexes are of the integer type and all item values have a common type
requirements.canonical: An index notation used for automatic typing in which all indexes are of the `integer` type and all item values have a common type SHALL provide the automatic type `record of` the common type.
requirements.original: k) Index assignment notation where all indexes are of the integer type and all item values have a common type shall provide an automatic type record of _{common type}.

ambiguity.issue: "index assignment notation" is used for the glossary term "index notation".

requirements.subject: ent:common-type
requirements.canonical: The common type of the item values of an index notation with integer indexes used for automatic typing SHALL fulfil the requirements for automatic typing.
requirements.original: The common type shall fulfil requirements_ for automatic typing.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.condition: all indexes have a common non-integer type and all item values have a common type
requirements.canonical: An index notation used for automatic typing in which all indexes have a common type other than `integer` and all item values have a common type SHALL provide the automatic type `map from` the common index type `to` the common value type.
requirements.original: l) Index assignment notation where all indexes have a common type in case the type is different from the integer type and all item values have a common type shall provide an automatic type map from _{common type of the indexes} to_ _{common type of the values}.

ambiguity.issue: "index assignment notation" is used for the glossary term "index notation".

requirements.subject: ent:common-type
requirements.canonical: The common type of the indexes and the common type of the item values of an index notation with non-integer indexes used for automatic typing SHALL fulfil the requirements for automatic typing.
requirements.original: The common type of the indexes and the_ common type of the values shall fulfil requirements for automatic typing.

requirements.subject: ent:template-list
requirements.condition: all templates in the list have a common type
requirements.canonical: A template list with two or more items or a complemented template list, in which all templates have a common type, SHALL provide an automatic type equal to the common type.
requirements.original: m) List of templates with two or more items and complemented list of templates where all templates have a common type shall provide automatic type that is equal to the common type.

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether "with two or more items" also applies to the complemented list, and "and" means "or" here. Chose the reading that the minimum of two items applies only to the template list.
readings: A template list with two or more items, or a complemented template list with any number of items, SHALL provide the common type as automatic type.
A template list or a complemented template list SHALL provide the common type as automatic type only if it has two or more items.

requirements.subject: ent:common-type
requirements.canonical: The common type of the templates of a template list or complemented template list used for automatic typing SHALL fulfil the requirements for automatic typing.
requirements.original: The common type shall fulfil requirements for automatic typing.

requirements.subject: ent:automatic-type-initializer
requirements.canonical: The template body used for automatic typing MAY be a value range.
requirements.original: n) Value range.

requirements.subject: ent:value-range
requirements.canonical: The automatic type of a value range IS equal to the type of its bounds.
requirements.original: The automatic type is equal to the type of the bounds.

ambiguity.issue: The rule does not say what happens when one bound is infinity or when the bounds have different types. Chose the reading that the type of the non-infinite bound(s) is used.
readings: The automatic type of a value range IS the type of its finite bound(s); bounds of different types are an error.
The automatic type of a value range IS the common type of both bounds, determined by the expression rules.

requirements.subject: ent:value-range
requirements.condition: both bounds are set to infinity
requirements.canonical: If both bounds of a value range used for automatic typing are infinity, the automatic type IS `integer`.
requirements.original: If both bounds are set to infinity, the integer type is provided.

requirements.subject: ent:automatic-type-initializer
requirements.canonical: The template body used for automatic typing MAY be a pattern.
requirements.original: o) Pattern.

requirements.subject: ent:pattern
requirements.condition: the pattern contains only characters or references of the charstring type
requirements.canonical: If a pattern used for automatic typing contains only characters or references of the `charstring` type, the automatic type IS `charstring`.
requirements.original: If the pattern contains only characters or references of the charstring type, the automatic type is charstring, otherwise it is universal charstring.

requirements.subject: ent:pattern
requirements.condition: the pattern contains a character or reference not of the charstring type
requirements.canonical: If a pattern used for automatic typing contains a character or reference that is not of the `charstring` type, the automatic type IS `universal charstring`.
requirements.original: If the pattern contains only characters or references of the charstring type, the automatic type is charstring, otherwise it is universal charstring.

requirements.subject: ent:superset-subset
requirements.condition: all items have a common type
requirements.canonical: A `superset` or `subset` matching mechanism in which all items have a common type SHALL provide the automatic type `set of` the common type.
requirements.original: p) Superset and subset where all items have a common type shall provide an automatic type set of _{common_ _type}.

ambiguity.issue: "Superset and subset" means either of the two matching mechanisms.

requirements.subject: ent:common-type
requirements.canonical: The common type of the items of a `superset` or `subset` matching mechanism used for automatic typing SHALL fulfil the requirements for automatic typing.
requirements.original: The common type shall fulfil requirements for automatic typing._ q) Any other TTCN-3 language operation that can occur on the right-hand side of an assignment where the type context is unambiguous.

requirements.subject: ent:automatic-type-initializer
requirements.canonical: The expression or template body used for automatic typing MAY be any other TTCN-3 language operation that can occur on the right-hand side of an assignment, if its type context is unambiguous.
requirements.original: The common type shall fulfil requirements for automatic typing._ q) Any other TTCN-3 language operation that can occur on the right-hand side of an assignment where the type context is unambiguous.

ambiguity.issue: With an automatic type there is no declared type that provides a type context, so it is unclear which operations qualify; the item is open-ended. Chose the reading that the operation itself must determine its type unambiguously.
readings: Any operation whose result type is determined by the operation itself MAY be used for automatic typing.
Any operation MAY be used for automatic typing if an enclosing construct provides an unambiguous type context.

requirements.subject: ent:automatic-type-initializer
requirements.canonical: The template body of a declaration that uses the automatic type SHALL NOT consist only of the AnyValue matching symbol `?`, because `?` does not provide a type.
requirements.original: var template v_automaticErr := ?; // Causes an error as the ? symbol doesn't provide a type
